scope_rule: Claims are valid only for the stated data contract, information contract and evaluation regime.

entries.claim: The input-only GRU learns the smooth subthreshold manifold substantially better than event waveforms.
limitations: single trained seed in factorial 11
implications: preserve subthreshold fidelity as a guardrail

entries.claim: Many synaptic and slow internal coordinates are predictable even when the voltage spike regime collapses.
limitations: state-family averages hide coordinate outliers
implications: always report per-family and worst-coordinate guardrails

entries.claim: Every factorial-11 cell misses every teacher spike.
quantitative_signature: 0/102 predicted spikes in all four cells
limitations: threshold-based event definition
implications: factorial cells cannot be promoted

entries.claim: The dominant spike failure is amplitude collapse, not merely temporal jitter.
quantitative_signature: predictions remain near or below -58 mV
limitations: does not locate the causal mechanism
implications: diagnose imbalance, gradient conflict and latent accessibility before timing refinements

entries.claim: The learned voltage has almost no high-frequency power relative to the teacher.
quantitative_signature: above-200 Hz ratio near 0.00025 for GRU-MRSTFT
limitations: spectral ratios do not identify phase or event alignment
implications: retain spectral metrics as diagnosis, not as sole objective

entries.claim: MR-STFT improves common and slow regimes on the GRU scaffold.
limitations: single seed
not a spike recovery
implications: MR-STFT is a useful spectral auxiliary but not a complete event objective

entries.claim: MR-STFT is insufficient for rare fast transitions and can trade away synaptic-state accuracy.
limitations: one weighting and one scaffold
implications: close sufficiency claim; keep weights/objective form as separate open questions

entries.claim: The tested 7.5 ms causal dilated frontend degrades the baseline and fails spike recovery.
limitations: does not falsify all convolutional or ConvGRU architectures
implications: reject only this frontend-contract pair

entries.claim: Explicitly event-centred optimizer exposure is very sparse in factorial 11.
limitations: ordinary windows can also contain events
implications: measure effective event exposure and gradient contribution before changing the sampler

entries.claim: Broad spike-support regime information is decodable from the recurrent representation.
quantitative_signature: auxiliary phase/router tasks respond to event support
limitations: broad regime decoding does not imply exact phase/amplitude accessibility
implications: distinguish representation presence from usable readout geometry

entries.claim: A residual TCN can localize some events but broad corrections destroy subthreshold guardrails.
quantitative_signature: 23 predicted, 14 matched of 136 teacher spikes, F1 0.176
limitations: different evaluation archive from factorial 11
implications: event localization and amplitude correction should be diagnosed separately

entries.claim: A learned gate identifies event support, while the associated residual expert fails to learn the required correction.
limitations: one residual parameterization and training recipe
implications: do not infer that mixture routing alone solves the waveform

entries.claim: Narrowing residual support reduces spill but removes recovered spikes.
quantitative_signature: subthreshold protection improves while spike recovery disappears
limitations: single support rule
implications: support localization and correction capacity form a measured trade-off

entries.claim: Previously tested derivative/event-aware penalties did not by themselves prevent smooth-regime collapse.
quantitative_signature: broad plateau or auxiliary-task success without waveform recovery
limitations: does not falsify every derivative-aware objective
implications: new losses require a distinct mechanism and preregistered signature

entries.claim: Historical state-feedback experiments support partial, not total, subsystem modularity.
quantitative_signature: selected receptor transitions benefited from local GRU modules; other coordinates required a global backbone
limitations: different teacher and privileged state-feedback contract
implications: modular candidates need monolithic and information-contract controls

entries.claim: At least one historical coordinate was not autonomous under a local-only decomposition.
limitations: coordinate indexing belongs to older 17-state contract
implications: ontology does not imply statistical independence

entries.claim: Excellent one-step voltage accuracy does not guarantee stable long autoregressive rollout.
quantitative_signature: one-step test voltage RMSE 0.0264 mV; horizon-dependent drift remained a separate property
limitations: older teacher and feedback contract
implications: rollout stability must be an independent metric and training axis

entries.claim: Predicted physical-state feedback may expose fast phase information unavailable to an input-only readout.
limitations: must avoid teacher-state leakage after initialization
implications: run SR-01 only after DG-02

entries.claim: The current enriched dataset has a fixed auditable identity and trajectory-disjoint evaluation contract.
limitations: hash establishes identity, not physiological completeness
implications: all comparisons must record the exact hash

entries.claim: A single event-voltage RMSE is insufficient to characterize transition learning.
quantitative_signature: amplitude collapse, event count, spectral loss and slow-state trade-offs can diverge
limitations: metric battery still requires calibration
implications: use event precision/recall, peak amplitude, phase, spectral power, rollout and state-family guardrails together

entries.claim: Rare-event gradients are present and usable when event-centred windows are shown to every factorial-11 checkpoint.
entries.scope: DG-01; four frozen single-seed checkpoints; six event windows from three validation trajectories
limitations: six event windows are not independent; two trajectory pairs overlap
gradient existence does not prove sufficient representation or expressivity
implications: gradient absence is not the dominant global explanation
run DG-02 before changing the information contract

entries.claim: The current target distribution is extremely imbalanced and conditional voltage error rises as target density falls.
quantitative_signature: median target-density versus RMSE rank correlation -0.944
GRU-MSE RMSE rises from 0.92 mV in the dense -70 to -66 mV bin to 97.89 mV in the 20 to 60 mV bin
limitations: density and exposure are correlated in this observational diagnostic
causal attribution requires a controlled objective/sampler experiment
implications: H-LOSS-02 is supported diagnostically
retain LO-02 as an authorized causal branch after DG-02

entries.claim: The optimizer devotes very little explicit update mass to event-centred windows despite their usable gradients.
entries.scope: DG-01 audit of factorial-11 training and validation gradients
limitations: ordinary natural windows can contain events
does not isolate sampler from objective weighting
implications: H-TRAIN-01 is supported diagnostically
retain TR-01 as an authorized causal branch after DG-02

entries.claim: Gradient conflict is architecture- and block-specific rather than a stable global explanation of spike collapse.
limitations: six windows per view
one checkpoint seed
block cosines vary strongly by architecture and objective
implications: do not authorize a universal PCGrad/conflict-loss branch
retain block-specific conflict as a secondary DG-02 question

entries.claim: Training paths strongly reduce common, subthreshold and synaptic losses while barely reducing event loss.
quantitative_signature: event loss falls only about 9-15% from initialization to checkpoint
paired MSE-to-MR-STFT paths leave event loss almost flat
limitations: interpolation recomputes only the last 512 packed context steps
a parameter-space path is descriptive rather than a causal training trajectory
implications: the learned solution allocates capacity toward dense regimes
objective/exposure interventions have stronger support than blind capacity scaling
